# Federal Reserve and Independent Agencies

## By the end of today

You will be able to explain why some government power is insulated from short-term politics, and what trade-offs that insulation creates.

## Where this fits

The executive implements policy. Some implementation is deliberately placed **outside** ordinary presidential control.

## What the fight is really about

Full faith and credit is a public good. Brinkmanship taxes it.

Douglass North: credible commitment is a development technology. Governments that reliably pay their debts make long-term investment rational.

## Why a Federal Reserve

Lender of last resort after repeated panics. Elastic currency. A bank for the government that is not simply the President’s checking account.

## Dual mandate

Maximum employment and stable prices.

## Independence — the design

Congress sets the goals. The Fed chooses day-to-day means. Governors: 14-year staggered terms. Not a fourth branch. Created by Congress. Oversight remains.

## Grain of truth, then the rest

Regional banks and member-bank stock exist. Jekyll Island was secretive. Policy mistakes are real. None of that equals a private family owning the money supply. Excess earnings are remitted to the U.S. Treasury.

## The standing trade-off

Insulation can protect long-term goods. Insulation can also hide mistakes and weaken democratic control.

## Discussion

1. Should monetary policy be as insulated as judicial review, less so, or not at all?
2. When is “audit the Fed” a transparency demand, and when is it a bid to take over the dual mandate?
3. What other agencies, if any, should be this insulated?
